name: Max King
life: “I still remember a tomato plant surviving three shift changes.” On Wednesday, near the market by Market Flats, Max often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I have covered my partner's Saturdays for a decade. My own card names the neighbor who waters my tomatoes.
appearance: Max has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Look for a high puff tied with plain cord. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a plum-colored cardigan with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. In conversation Max starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak.
personality: Max prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To bring tomatoes to the neighbor who watered them.
family: Helena Neal is Max’s cousin raised in the same household. Max is free to hang up first. Helena makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The pawned trumpet*, Helena says, “I took the loan to get home for my mother's funeral.”
connections: Milan Gray. A late taxi escort and a neighbor watering tomatoes reveal the second shift behind an ordinary watch.

reactions.situation: A neighbor named on several cards asks for a favor in return
reactions.response: Max asks the neighbor what kind of help they actually need now.

reactions.response: Max asks one close relative to check in privately instead of stopping the party for a public inquiry.
